newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish Islamists agree conditionally on handover.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Islamists agree conditionally on handover.

text.p: Turkey's ruling Islamists have conditionally agreed to hand over power to their pro-Western coalition allies later this week, a spokesman for Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Welfare Party said on Monday.
"We have reached an agreement to leave office on June 18. There are, of course, conditions. We will go ahead with what we have promised to do," spokesman Oguzhan Asilturk told a news conference.

Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller, head of Erbakan's True Path Party coalition partner, said earlier the prime minister would step down within a few days in a row with the army over Islamist activism.

Welfare has asked Ciller to cooperate on legislation to take the country to early polls in return for giving the top job to Ciller. The Islamists, facing closure as a party by the constitutional court for alleged religious militancy, also want to see True Path help pass a law to prevent them being banned.
Erbakan and Ciller earlier announced they would swap jobs by the end of this month and form a caretaker government to go for early elections. No date for the polls was set.

The planned power transfer and early polls would have to overcome the obstacles of presidential and parliamentary approval. The coalition lacks a majority in the national assembly after defections and resignations.
